exposure: Post-output review with access to all responses, original reference and earlier results interpretation. No independent or sealed human review.
scope: All 22 mismatches grouped into nine card-dimension issues; selective review is not a full reference validation.

items.basis: E2 establishes cancellation before execution, beyond receipt alone. The objective is interruption, but the mitigation question never names a consequence distinct from cancellation. The reference assumes that distinction.
items.successor_requirement: Specify the consequence and its observation window separately from the stop objective. Include cancellation with and without consequence evidence.

items.basis: E2 establishes non-delivery. No observed consequence is specified. A failed necessary route may support absence of effect through that route, but the packet does not define exclusivity or the outcome proposition sufficiently to settle that inference.
items.successor_requirement: Specify the bounded consequence, possible alternative routes and what affirmative failure evidence is required.

items.basis: E1 records sending. E2 and E3 conflict over receipt and execution; neither contradicts the console attempt. The action question explicitly includes attempts.
items.successor_requirement: Preserve the attempt/receipt distinction and add a separate case with an actual contradiction about issuance.

items.basis: E2 and E3 contradict cancellation versus execution. That is outcome-relevant if cancellation is the selected outcome. No separate consequence is defined, so the original reference depends on an unstated boundary.
items.successor_requirement: Separate trajectory change from the specified consequence and test conflict at each level.

items.basis: E1-E3 repeat sending and supply no receipt. The reference is supported by the intended downstream-receipt reading, but partial could be read as one segment of a transmission path. The extent of the proposition needs explicit scope.
items.successor_requirement: Define partial over named downstream targets or required subclaims; sending alone does not establish any target receipt. Compare C02 and C06 prospectively.

items.basis: E2 restricts receipt records. It does not identify withheld consequence records. The reference uses dimension-specific silence, while the model may propagate an upstream evidence barrier to the whole causal claim. The rule does not explicitly resolve overlapping missingness.
items.successor_requirement: Record barriers by dimension and specify treatment when causal linkage and outcome observation have different missingness states.

items.basis: E2 is supplied but its identity fields are unreadable. The reference treats linkage as residual ambiguity; the codebook also allows unresolved states under documented access conditions. Unreadability is not cleanly separated from restricted access.
items.successor_requirement: Define treatment of damaged or unreadable fields separately from withheld records, with paired cases.

items.basis: E2 reports unreadable receipt identity fields and no mapping. Consequences are not reported. A barrier to linking the action does not specify whether consequence evidence exists. The missingness precedence is incomplete.
items.successor_requirement: Specify dimension-local missingness and preserve multiple limitations in rationale rather than automatically copying a label downstream.

items.basis: E2 records receipt at W only. It reports neither cancellation nor a consequence at either worker. The question expressly says downstream acknowledgement does not establish mitigation.
items.successor_requirement: Retain this boundary; add receipt-only, executed-stop and observed-consequence variants for the same named outcome.
